messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a regression on canary after runtime-driver v2.7 roll. p50 token latency up ~22% for long sequences (>2048). Root trace points to KV cache misses + switching to fallback kernel path.
priya: Ugh. Is this reproing locally or only on canary/dedicated?
alex: Only on canary so far, but it's consistent across 3 nodes in the canary pool. Short sequences (<512) unaffected.
marco: I ran a quick profile earlier. Looks like the kernel selector is choosing the 'generic_attn' path for seqlen bins > 2048 instead of the optimized 'block_attn_v2' for a subset of models (gpt-like, kv-quantized). That increases per-token op time.
eva: Any change to the cache keying scheme in the v2.7 driver? If keys drift, cache becomes cold and kernel warmup happens more often.
alex: Yes — v2.7 changed key prefix to include driver BuildID to force clean cache on major runtime upgrade. That was intentional for old issues, but seems to be causing a lot of churn for canary traffic.
marco: Also saw that persistence TTL default got flipped from "persistent" -> "session" in the same roll, so keys don't survive driver restart.
priya: So two things: (1) keys are getting invalidated due to BuildID in key, (2) smaller TTL meaning missing persisted KV. Combined -> cache miss storm.
eva: That explains more cache misses and more kernel selection happening cold. Kernel selector uses a small LRU of past picks per model+seqbin; if cache cold it falls back to conservative kernel.
alex: Profiling snippet:
```
# perf summary (canary-node-7)
p50 token time: 18.2ms (was 14.9ms)
cache hit rate (prefix KV): 61% (was 92%)
kernel switch rate (per request): 0.31 -> 0.78
```
marco: I dumped the KV keyspace and confirmed ~2.4M new keys with BuildID suffix, vs 400k previously. Key distribution skewed towards long prefixes.
priya: What's a minimal mitigation we can push quickly? Revert BuildID inclusion? Change TTL to persistent? Hotfix key normalization?
eva: Short-term: revert the BuildID suffix and restore persistent TTL for persisted cache. Medium-term: change key scheme to include stable model fingerprint + quant/profile hash but exclude ephemeral driver build identifier; add migration marker to allow detection of genuine incompatible schema changes.
marco: I sketched a key function earlier — propose stable_key = sha1(model_fingerprint + quant_profile + kernel_family) — avoid driver/build identifiers. Example: 
```
func stableKey(modelFingerprint, quantProfile, kernelFamily string) string {
  input := fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%s", modelFingerprint, quantProfile, kernelFamily)
  return sha1sum(input)
}
```
alex: PR #5123 attempts a minimal rollback of the BuildID suffix and sets persist TTL for canary nodes. Deployed to canary at 15:42. deploy-bot: deploy v2.7-rollback started (canary pool).
deploy-bot: canary deploy complete: v2.7-rollback @ 15:49.
srebot: Alert suppression: temporarily silenced KV-miss alerts for canary to avoid noise during debugging.
priya: After rollback, can you re-run the synthetic long-seq load? We need numbers.
marco: Ran synthetic test (10 workers, 1k requests each) after rollback:
```
post-rollback p50: 15.1ms
cache hit rate: 89%
kernel switch rate: 0.28
```
eva: That's much better and close to baseline. Still want to follow-up: make key scheme explicit in docs and add a migration verifier that can detect when we intentionally invalidate keys.
alex: Agreed. Action items:
- marco: open PR to change keying scheme to stableKey + migration flag (owner: marco, PR #5127)
- eva: add migration verifier + docs + tests (PR #5130)
- priya: prepare canary plan for staged rollout and perf gating (run synthetic regression suite)
- infra: consider adding an opt-in BuildID flag for full cache flush only when customer explicitly requests.
marco: I'll also add histogram metrics for per-model seqlen-bin kernel choices so we can alert earlier.
priya: Thanks — if no objection I'll mark the canary rollback as resolved and proceed with the follow-ups.
alex: No objections. Marking resolved, keeping thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
